title: 1976 AHSME Problem 26
statement: In the adjoining figure, every point of circle \(O'\) is exterior to circle \(O.\) Let \(P\) and \(Q\) be the points of intersection of an internal common tangent with the two external common tangents. Then the length of \(PQ\) is

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
the average of the lengths of the internal and external common
tangents

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
equal to the length of an external common tangent if and only
if circles \(O\) and \(O'\) have equal radii

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
always equal to the length of an external
common tangent

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: greater than the length of an external common tangent

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
the geometric mean of the lengths of the internal and external
common tangents

solutions.text:
Let the internal tangent touch \(O\) and \(O'\) at \(R\) and \(S.\) Let the external tangent through \(P\) touch them at \(X\) and \(Y,\) and let the one through \(Q\) touch them at \(V\) and \(W.\) Equal tangent segments from a point give \[ \begin{gathered} PR=PX,\\ PS=PY,\\ QR=QV,\\ QS=QW. \end{gathered} \] Along the internal tangent, \(PR+QR=PQ\) and \(PS+QS=PQ.\) Adding, \[ \begin{aligned} PR+QR+PS+QS=2PQ. \end{aligned} \] Along the external tangents, \(PX+PY=XY\) and \(QV+QW=VW.\) Therefore \(2PQ=XY+VW.\) The two external common tangent segments have equal length, so \(XY=VW\) and hence \(PQ=XY=VW.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Mark the tangency point on each of the three tangent lines
From either \(P\) or \(Q,\) tangent segments to the same circle have equal lengths
